title: Idolatry and Conscience
english: The faithful are being persuaded to observe legalistic rules and to practice a form of voluntary worship, which is actually a deceitful and ancient practice, pouring out the poison of this ancient deceit to the simpler souls, and convincing them to observe days and months, and to choose other things to fulfill, and advising them to select other things to complete their observance.

Since, then, we were bought with a price, not with perishable silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, who is without blemish and spotless (1 Peter 1:19), we ought to be subject to his laws.

The Corinthian church was convinced that God is one and only, and that idols are not gods, and they ridiculed those who sacrificed to them, saying that the sacrifices are nothing, and they ate them without distinction, not considering any defilement from this.

However, they scandalized the weak who thought that they should not participate in the festivals of the idols, and for this reason, Paul cuts off these things, wanting the faithful to be monotonous, serving only the all-holy God.

We know that there is no idol in the world, and that those who do not know the idols at all, or who know them accurately as mere wood and stone, do not consider them worthy of any word, but rather believe in one God and Father from whom all things are, and in one Lord Jesus Christ through whom all things are.

The glory of God's lordship and the excellence of the one born from Him are not to be understood in the same way as the many gods and lords that are called such in the Spirit, which knowledge few have, for there are many gods and lords, and many are called gods and lords according to the worthiness of participation in the Holy Spirit.

Unfortunately, many people, even some who have believed in Christ, still consider many gods to exist and have not completely abandoned the customs of idolatry, and some, with a conscience still weak, eat food offered to idols and their conscience is defiled.

It is necessary to guide the weak with spiritual teachings, not to eat indiscriminately and sit with the unbelievers, but rather to do everything in a becoming manner, using our authority with discernment and not on all occasions or at all times, lest our authority become a stumbling block to the weak.

For being indifferent about eating food offered to idols and sitting with the unbelievers in the temples can give an occasion for scandal, showing off their own stability, and thus sinning against brothers and striking their weak conscience, we sin against Christ.

By causing our brothers to stumble, we will be held accountable for our actions against Christ, who died for the salvation of all people, and the consequences of our actions are severe: the weak brother perishes because of our knowledge, and what is good for us becomes a source of sin, while the steadfastness of our faith becomes a scandal to our brothers, and our knowledge becomes a pit.

This is a deeply painful reality, and we should not overlook the weaknesses of our brothers or fail to support their fragile consciences, but rather be mindful of the need to avoid putting stumbling blocks or scandals in the way of our brothers, recognizing the importance of considering their well-being, and remembering that we must not put a stumbling block or scandal before a brother (Romans 14:13).

title: Spiritual Nourishment
english: We are warned not to despise any of the little ones, for their angels always behold the face of the Father, and if we neglect the weaknesses of our brethren, we will be accused by the holy angels, as if we are neglecting their weaknesses and not rather making every effort to support their weakness, being conscious of it.

Our fathers were all under the cloud, and Paul teaches us that eating things sacrificed to idols is not beneficial but rather dangerous, and that it is not without harm for those who are accustomed to do wrong to attack, for it brings about doing what is not lawful, as the human mind is easily led astray to what is not proper, and it receives not a beautiful image of the matter, but rather a very similar one, the things that happened to the Israelites who came from blood in the wilderness, as it is written (1 Corinthians 10:1-5).

The Israelites were perfected through the cloud in the sea, with Moses mediating, and they ate the bread from heaven and drank the life-giving drink, for Christ himself, being the rock, nourished them, and although he suffered death voluntarily, he is unbroken as God, and we say that such things are prefigurations of spiritual matters.

The elders were corrupted in Sattin, where they served idols and were devoted to Beelphagor, and this corruption led to a clash with the idolaters, despite the fact that they had been baptized in the cloud and in the sea, and had eaten the bread from heaven and drunk the spiritual drink, and they were corrupted, having become mixed with the idolaters, and having fallen into apostasy, as they fellowshipped and shared in the idolatrous table, they easily fell into apostasy and danced with women, as the prophet had warned (Numbers 25:1-3).

Solomon's words are relevant here: 'The one who walks with the wise will be wise, but the one who walks with the foolish will be known' (Proverbs 13:20), and we too, before our faith in Christ, were yoked to the demons' greed and served the spiritual Pharaoh, that is, Satan, and we vainly gave him honor, like clay and brick, being occupied with the works of the flesh, and being led astray, exchanging the truth for a lie.

But Christ Jesus, the mediator between God and men, gave himself as a ransom for all, and led us through the turbulent sea of this life, perfecting us through holy baptism, and he is the cloud from above, providing living water to those who love him, and this living water is the Spirit, as Christ himself said, 'He who believes in me, as the Scripture has said, will have rivers of living water flowing from his heart' (John 7:38), and the evangelist explains that this refers to the Spirit that believers would soon receive.

We, too, have partaken of the truly life-giving bread and have drunk the spiritual drink, just as the Israelites drank water from the rock in the wilderness, and the rock was Christ, who is our source of spiritual nourishment, and we have been led through the sea of this life, and have been initiated through holy baptism.
